chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) on the Janazah (funeral prayer), is there a fixed number for it or not? He said, 'No. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say it eleven times, nine times, seven times, five times, six times, and four times.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains regarding the addition of Takbir beyond five times is set aside by consensus. It is permissible that he (peace be upon him) informed about the action of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in this manner because he would say Takbir on one funeral or two, so when another funeral was brought, he would start from where he had finished, [having] five Takbirat. So if added to what he had already said, he would exceed five Takbirat, and that is permissible as we will clarify later, God willing. As for what it contains regarding four Takbirat, it is attributed to Taqiyya (dissimulation) because that is the opinion of the opponents, or he informed about the action of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with the hypocrites and those suspected of Islam, because he (peace be upon him) used to do so. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of Takbirat in the Shia funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the number of Takbirat during Salat al-Janazah, citing variations from four to eleven reported from Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The commentary by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan distinguishes between the permissibility of exceeding five Takbirat through consecutive prayers and the attribution of the four-Takbir count to Taqiyya or specific contexts like praying with hypocrites, reflecting the jurisprudential nuance in Shia tradition.
